profile.subtitleJa: ツェルヤの子、アドニヤを支持した人物
profile.summaryJa: ヨアブはツェルヤの子として名が挙げられ、祭司アビヤタルとともにアドニヤを支持したと記されています。

facts.textJa: バテ・シェバは、ヨアブが王の子たちと祭司アビヤタルを伴って集まる一方、ソロモンは呼ばれなかったと伝えます。
ダビデはソロモンに、ヨアブがアブネルとアマサを殺したことを思い起こさせます。
アドニヤの死の知らせを聞いたヨアブは、主の天幕へ逃れました。
ヨアブは天幕から出ることを拒み、そこで死ぬと言いました。
ソロモンは、ヨアブとその子孫に血の責任が戻ると述べます。
ヨアブは軍の長としてエドムへ進み、イスラエル軍とともにしばらく滞在しました。
ハダドはエジプトで、ダビデと軍の長ヨアブが死んだと聞いたと記されます。

wikipedia.noteJa: 記事はツェルヤの子ヨアブを扱います。本書のアドニヤ支持、ダビデの指示、天幕での最期にも触れるため、本書最後の言及まで表示を遅らせています。

primaryWitnesses.textualBasisJa: He conferred with Joab the son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest; and they followed Adonijah and helped him.
He has slain cattle and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and has called all the sons of the king, Abiathar the priest, and Joab the captain of the army; but he hasn’t called Solomon your servant.
Adonijah and all the guests who were with him heard it as they had finished eating. When Joab heard the sound of the trumpet, he said, “Why is this noise of the city being in an uproar?”

“Moreover you know also what Joab the son of Zeruiah did to me, even what he did to the two captains of the armies of Israel, to Abner the son of Ner and to Amasa the son of Jether, whom he killed, and shed the blood of war in peace, and put the blood of war on his sash that was around his waist and in his sandals that were on his feet.

King Solomon answered his mother, “Why do you ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask for him the kingdom also, for he is my elder brother; even for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab the son of Zeruiah.”
This news came to Joab; for Joab had followed Adonijah, although he didn’t follow Absalom. Joab fled to the LORD’s Tent, and held onto the horns of the altar.
King Solomon was told, “Joab has fled to the LORD’s Tent; and behold, he is by the altar.” Then Solomon sent Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, saying, “Go, fall on him.”

Benaiah came to the LORD’s Tent, and said to him, “The king says, ‘Come out!’” He said, “No; but I will die here.” Benaiah brought the king word again, saying, “This is what Joab said, and this is how he answered me.”
The king said to him, “Do as he has said, and fall on him, and bury him, that you may take away the blood, which Joab shed without cause, from me and from my father’s house.

So their blood will return on the head of Joab and on the head of his offspring forever. But for David, for his offspring, for his house, and for his throne, there will be peace forever from the LORD.”
For when David was in Edom, and Joab the captain of the army had gone up to bury the slain, and had struck every male in Edom
(for Joab and all Israel remained there six months, until he had cut off every male in Edom),
When Hadad heard in Egypt that David slept with his fathers, and that Joab the captain of the army was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, “Let me depart, that I may go to my own country.”
